import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """date,time,product,size,price,quantity,payment_method,customer_age_group,is_takeaway,total
2024-01-01,00:00,Cappuccino,Large,4.18,2,Credit Card,55+,1,8.36
2024-01-01,02:00,Cappuccino,Medium,4.01,3,Credit Card,35-44,1,12.03
2024-01-01,04:00,Tea,Small,5.22,1,Credit Card,18-24,1,5.22
2024-01-01,06:00,Latte,Large,6.37,2,Credit Card,45-54,1,12.74
2024-01-01,08:00,Americano,Medium,7.07,3,Cash,45-54,1,21.21
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# --- Create the visualization ---

# Set a professional and clean style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a bar plot showing total sales per transaction, colored by product
ax = sns.barplot(
    data=df,
    x='time',
    y='total',
    hue='product',
    palette='magma',
    dodge=False  # Keep bars centered as there's one per time slot
)

# Add value labels on top of each bar for clarity
for p in ax.patches:
    ax.annotate(
        f'${p.get_height():.2f}',
        (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
        ha='center',
        va='center',
        xytext=(0, 10),
        textcoords='offset points',
        fontsize=12,
        fontweight='medium'
    )

# Customize titles and labels for a polished look
plt.title('Early Morning Sales by Transaction (Jan 1, 2024)', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Time of Transaction', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
plt.ylabel('Total Sale Amount ($)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Adjust tick parameters for readability
plt.xticks(fontsize=12)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)

plt.legend(title='Product', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11', loc='upper left')

# Use a tight layout to ensure all elements are visible
plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
